population: SYNTHETIC + DEVELOPMENT -- no holdout opened, nothing adjudicated, nothing scored
question: can every score_metrics obligation be satisfied from committed artifacts, with no PDF access, no runner access, no text matching, and no implementation-time choice?
note: PAGE_LIMIT is a machinery demonstration window, not a census
artifacts_created: NONE of frames.json, oracle_key.json, oracle_blind.json, oracle_adjudicated.json, metrics.json, scores.json, EXECUTION-START.json

bilateral_gate.limit: one skeleton by A19 -- both runners call run_hybrid.neutral_skeleton; this gate catches divergence in what each arm RETURNS, not two independent derivations

genuine_unmatched.lever: merged-line text perturbation -> MERGE_RECONSTRUCTION_MISMATCH; placement reads print_lines/emitted and is unaffected

H.rule0_comparison: RAW FACTS ONLY -- Rule 0 margin-line interpretation frozen by A39.1 (count of Page.lines where line_number is not None; any positive deficit fires); application belongs to the later architecture decision

X.rule0_comparison: RAW FACTS ONLY -- Rule 0 margin-line interpretation frozen by A39.1 (count of Page.lines where line_number is not None; any positive deficit fires); application belongs to the later architecture decision

resolved_ambiguities.ruling: margin_lines_recovered = count of Page.lines where line_number is not None; any strictly positive per-document deficit fires; no tolerance. The glyph-size count and per-line keys remain diagnostics and do not determine the clause.

tests.test: every committed neutral line's candidates are EXACTLY its gids
tests.fails_when: a gid has no candidate, or a candidate names a gid outside the line -- either way the A30.3 resolver would search the wrong glyph set

tests.test: the candidate population is non-empty, so the check above is not vacuous
tests.fails_when: no line carries candidates, so 'all lines agree' passed on nothing

tests.test: no candidate exists outside the committed gid sets (U+0020 among them)
tests.fails_when: a candidate was invented from a source glyph the skeleton rejected, e.g. a word space

tests.test: candidate x0 is UNROUNDED source geometry
tests.fails_when: every x0 lands on a 4-decimal grid, i.e. it was rounded for serialization -- rounding here can move a nearest-glyph decision

tests.test: candidates serialize in ngid order (determinism ONLY, never reading order)
tests.fails_when: serialization order varies between runs, so the committed frame is not reproducible

tests.test: NEGATIVE -- mutating ONE arm's candidate x0 ABORTS frame construction
tests.fails_when: the arms' candidate geometry can diverge without the frame noticing, so the committed candidates would silently be whichever arm was read first

tests.test: ...and the UNMUTATED pair still builds, so the gate is not refusing everything
tests.fails_when: construction refuses even on clean input, making the control above meaningless

tests.test: both arms produced occurrence records
tests.fails_when: an arm produced no occurrences, so M1-M5 would have an empty emitted side

tests.test: every record is MATCHABLE or UNMATCHED and none is silently absent
tests.fails_when: a record carries neither status, i.e. an occurrence was dropped rather than reported

tests.test: a MATCHABLE record carries the A30 4-component occurrence key
tests.fails_when: the key is not the frozen (doc_sha, page, neutral_line_key, start_ngid) shape

tests.test: records are in DOCUMENT order, never ngid order
tests.fails_when: occurrences are ordered by ngid, which A30.1 forbids -- ngid order disagreed with printed order on 10 of 33,602 emitted lines

tests.test: the DEVELOPMENT material really does reuse region ordinals across pages
tests.fails_when: no ordinal repeats across pages here, so this material could not have exposed the contamination and the controls below would be vacuous

tests.test: EVERY private-key occurrence satisfies anchor.page == stimulus.page AND region == region
tests.fails_when: a stimulus carries an occurrence printed on another page or in another region, which would put headings the adjudicator never saw on the emitted side of the M1-M5 join

tests.test: NEGATIVE -- the retired region-ordinal-only filter DOES contaminate this material
tests.fails_when: the old filter happens to be equivalent here, so the repair is unproven and the control above passes for the wrong reason

tests.test: no architecture occurrence is duplicated into multiple PRIMARY stimuli
tests.fails_when: one emitted heading is counted in two regions, inflating the emitted set twice over

tests.test: a MATCHABLE occurrence's A30 key page AGREES with its stimulus page
tests.fails_when: the identity key names a different page from the stimulus carrying it, so the join would bind an adjudication to a heading printed elsewhere

tests.test: a GENUINE A30 refusal is UNMATCHED with an explicit reason
tests.fails_when: the perturbation did not actually induce an identity refusal, so this control proves nothing about how refusals are handled

tests.test: ...and it KEEPS its A28.5 physical page and region
tests.fails_when: an identity refusal erased the physical placement, so the occurrence would vanish from every region-scoped record and shrink an M1-M5 denominator invisibly

tests.test: the UNMATCHED occurrence SURVIVES into its exact stimulus
tests.fails_when: the refused occurrence reaches no private key at all, i.e. it was silently dropped

tests.test: ...and appears in NO other page/region
tests.fails_when: the refused occurrence also leaked into a stimulus for a different page or region

tests.test: every committed immediate_parent EQUALS production breadcrumb_for's penultimate element
tests.fails_when: the parent was derived by a NEW hierarchy walk that disagrees with production, so M4 would score the emitted side against a hierarchy production never produced

tests.test: the parent comparison is non-empty
tests.fails_when: no occurrence matched a production anchor, so the equality above compared nothing

tests.test: a root/no-parent case exists and is represented as null
tests.fails_when: no one-element breadcrumb appears, so the no-parent branch was never exercised

tests.test: M9 raw facts are committed for BOTH arms
tests.fails_when: a raw M9 quantity is missing, so score_metrics would have to rerun production anchor extraction to discover it

tests.test: the frozen coverage floor is production's own 0.85
tests.fails_when: the floor drifted from production's _COVERAGE_MIN, i.e. a threshold was invented here

tests.test: per-line margin keys are recorded, so a SET comparison stays possible
tests.fails_when: only counts are recorded, foreclosing the set-difference reading of Rule 0 before it has been ruled on

tests.test: this stage still records FACTS and does not APPLY Rule 0
tests.fails_when: frame construction applies the Rule 0 comparison, which belongs to the later architecture decision

tests.test: RULE0_MARGIN_LINE_QUANTITY is RESOLVED_BY_A39_1, and the ruling is implemented
tests.fails_when: the frozen A39.1 clause -- count of line_number is not None, ANY positive deficit fires, no tolerance -- is not what margin_line_loss implements, so the ledger would be claiming a resolution the code does not deliver

tests.test: the S1 sabotage scale is exactly the frozen 1.25
tests.fails_when: the scale drifted from the frozen value, or became a tunable dial

tests.test: S1 FIRES on DEVELOPMENT -- sabotage raises M0
tests.fails_when: advances x 1.25 does not raise the discordance count, which would mean M0 cannot detect a change it certainly should -- the comparator is not live

tests.test: ...and the sabotage really changed the input, so firing is not an artifact
tests.fails_when: the two runs report the same discordance, so nothing was actually sabotaged

tests.test: primary and sabotaged M0 are reported SEPARATELY
tests.fails_when: only one number is reported, so a reader cannot see what the control established

tests.test: the risk set is unchanged by sabotage, so only the TEXT moved
tests.fails_when: the sabotage moved the neutral skeleton, i.e. it changed the frame rather than the seam decision under test

tests.test: NEGATIVE -- a DEAD comparator (sabotage changes nothing) reports S1 FAIL
tests.fails_when: a comparator that cannot move still reports S1 firing, which is precisely the phase-1 defect S1 exists to catch

tests.test: the producer RUNS on a real DEVELOPMENT PDF without raising
tests.fails_when: the producer cannot execute at all -- which is how a nonexistent row key and the wrong denominator survived: nothing ever ran it on real measurements

tests.test: sampled pages equal the independently derived A39.2 sample
tests.fails_when: the producer measures a different page set from the frozen sample

tests.test: matched count and DENOMINATOR equal the direct x09 computation
tests.fails_when: the producer counts a different numerator or denominator than the frozen rule -- the exact defect: matched/pdfium instead of matched/max(pdfium, pymupdf)

tests.test: the whole GATE VERDICT equals X09.gate on the same rows
tests.fails_when: the producer's verdict differs from the frozen rule applied directly, i.e. it is recomputing the rule rather than calling it

tests.test: document fraction, worst page and pass all agree
tests.fails_when: a reported field disagrees with the gate that produced it

tests.test: cross-engine failure is NEVER decision-blocking
tests.fails_when: a cross-engine failure blocks the architecture decision, which A27.6 forbids

tests.test: PyMuPDF over-segmentation scores 100/120, not 100/100
tests.fails_when: the denominator is the PDFium count, so over-segmentation by the SECOND engine is invisible -- the control would report perfect agreement while the engines disagree

tests.test: PDFium over-segmentation scores 100/120 too -- the gate is SYMMETRIC
tests.fails_when: the gate favours one engine, so which engine over-segments changes the verdict

tests.test: ...and both are capable of FAILING the frozen thresholds
tests.fails_when: an 0.833 agreement passes, so the thresholds cannot see over-segmentation at all

tests.test: NEGATIVE -- a wrong document SHA REFUSES before any sample or measurement
tests.fails_when: a caller-supplied SHA that does not match the bytes selects a different page sample for the same document, silently and reproducibly

tests.test: ...and the correct SHA is accepted
tests.fails_when: verification refuses the real document, making the control above meaningless

tests.test: mutating a NON-sampled page changes nothing
tests.fails_when: an unsampled page reaches the gate, so this is not a 10 % sampled control at all

tests.test: ...while mutating a SAMPLED page DOES change the verdict
tests.fails_when: a sampled page cannot move the verdict, so sample membership is dead and the control above passed for the wrong reason

tests.test: an unsampled page exists, so the membership control is not vacuous
tests.fails_when: every page is sampled here, so 'unsampled changes nothing' was trivially true

tests.test: limit=None is a valid WHOLE-DOCUMENT call
tests.fails_when: the canonical writer's default path raises or silently measures a prefix -- a truncated confirmatory measurement would qualify a frame on a fraction of its pages

tests.test: ...and it measures MORE pages than the limited call, so None is not read as a prefix
tests.fails_when: limit=None produced the same page count as the limited run, i.e. it was reinterpreted

tests.test: EVERY listed score input is reachable from committed JSON, with no PDF or runner
tests.fails_when: a fact score_metrics needs survives only in a live Python object, so the scorer would have to reopen a PDF or rerun an architecture to get it

tests.test: NEGATIVE -- removing the occurrence records makes the reachability answer FALSE
tests.fails_when: the reachability check cannot detect a missing producer, so it would report success on an artifact chain that cannot actually feed the scorer
